UNIT TESTS (lib/compiler/objdump.sig, appended after the usage string):
- `test "murmur3_32 reference immediates"`: pins disasm.murmur3_32 against the SIMD-0178 reference immediates sol_log_=0x207559bd, sol_memcpy_=0x717cc4a3, sol_sha256=0x11f49d86, abort=0xb6fc1a11, sol_try_find_program_address=0x48504a38, sol_get_clock_sysvar=0xd56b5fe9, and ""==0x00000000.
- `test "sBPF decodeOne"`: hand-encodes REAL Solana sBPF opcodes and asserts the rendered asm string + returned stride for each via a std.Io.Writer.fixed buffer and w.buffered(), using a throwaway `disasm.Annotator{ .syms=&.{}, .syscalls=disasm.syscalls, .machine=.BPF }`:
  * mov r0, 0x2a   (0xb7, ALU64 mov imm) -> "mov r0, 0x2a", stride 8
  * mov r0, r1     (0xbf, ALU64 mov reg) -> "mov r0, r1", stride 8
  * add r1, 0x10   (0x07, ALU64 add imm) -> "add r1, 0x10", stride 8
  * ldxdw r0,[r1+0x8] (0x79, LDX dw)     -> "ldxdw r0, [r1+0x8]", stride 8
  * call 0x207559bd (0x85, src=0 static syscall; imm==murmur3(sol_log_)) -> "call 0x207559bd <sol_log_>", stride 8 (exercises Annotator.resolve against the comptime syscall table)
  * exit            (0x95)                -> "exit", stride 8
  * lddw r0, 0x1    (0x18 16-byte pair)   -> "lddw r0, 0x1", stride 16
  * a 2-byte short tail -> error.ParseFailure with "<truncated> 95 00" emitted first (no OOB read).

FEAT-003 DECODER BUGS CORRECTED HERE (authorized by the parent/user via workflow warning->answer; option 1 'fix the decoder now and pin correct Solana sBPF behavior'). While writing the decodeOne tests I found the FEAT-003 JMP decode table was mis-mapped vs the authoritative Solana sBPF table (anza-xyz/sbpf doc/bytecode.md, cross-checked against SIMD-0178): high-nibble ops must be 0x0 ja, 0x1 jeq, 0x2 jgt, 0x3 jge, 0x4 jset, 0x5 jne, 0x6 jsgt, 0x7 jsge, 0x8 call, 0x9 exit, 0xA jlt, 0xB jle, 0xC jslt, 0xD jsle (so real call=0x85, exit=0x95). The code had 0xc0=call/0xd0=exit (those are actually jslt/jsle) and the 0x4..0xd nibbles shifted, so real sBPF call/exit would mis-decode as jsgt/jsge and 0x85/0x95 were unrecognized. Two contained edits in the `disasm` namespace (ALU/LD/LDX/ST/STX decoding was already correct and left untouched):
  1. `jmpOp` rewritten to the authoritative nibble->mnemonic mapping above (with a doc comment citing anza-xyz/sbpf doc/bytecode.md).
  2. `decodeOne` JMP switch: exit is now the 0x90 nibble (0x95), call the 0x80 nibble (0x85). Added callx (0x8D, 0x80 nibble + src-reg bit 0x08) rendering as `callx <src>` so it no longer collides with `call` (0x85, src==0 static syscall per SIMD-0178).
Also folded in the FEAT-003 fix that FEAT-004 recorded as out-of-its-scope: the comptime `disasm.syscalls` murmur3 hash table tripped 'evaluation exceeded 1000 backwards branches', which made the JIT `sig objdump` command and `sig build-exe` fail before any format handler ran (only `sig test`, with a higher default quota, tolerated it). Added a minimal `@setEvalBranchQuota(20000)` inside that comptime `blk:` so the end-to-end objdump/build-exe path runs. These three edits are confined to the sBPF decoder + its quota; the COFF arm and the ELF/macho/wasm inspection paths were not touched.

SMOKE (end-to-end, now unblocked by the quota fix): built an x86_64-linux ELF object with `sig build-obj -target x86_64-linux` and ran the JIT objdump against it (SIG_LIB_DIR pointed at the worktree lib). `--summary` printed `type=REL machine=X86_64(62) ... class=ELF64 data=little flags=0x0 phnum=0 shnum=29`; `-s --file-headers` printed the full header view with va/size fields redacted to x's. The JIT path previously died at the comptime table; it now completes. (Smoke artifacts under .build/ were removed.)

SNAPSHOT/INTEGRATION (test/link.sig): added an `elf-objdump` case following the existing COFF verifyObjdump pattern (case.addObject with .sig_source_bytes exporting a global + an fn to get relocs/symbols, then four case.verifyObjdump calls under `-s`: --summary, --file-headers, --section-headers, --relocs, each with a distinct .sub_name and .arch=true). It is guarded by `if (ctx.target.result.ofmt == .elf)`.

SNAPSHOTS DEFERRED TO CI (rationale): the `test-link` matrix cannot produce ELF/sBPF binaries in this environment, so no new .dmp files were generated here and the ELF case does not fire on this Windows dev box:
  1. `link_targets` in test/tests.sig is Windows-ONLY (x86_64-windows gnu/msvc) -- there is no ELF/Linux target in the link matrix, so every verifyObjdump binary built today is COFF/PE. The ofmt==.elf guard keeps the new ELF case from running against a COFF binary (which would produce misleading snapshots). Adding a Linux target to link_targets would fix this but test/tests.sig is OUTSIDE this feature's allowed edit set.
  2. The worktree root build.sig does not even expose the `test-link` step (available steps: config:sig, sig, install-lib/sig, test); `addLinkTests`/`test-link` lives in test/tests.sig and is wired by the parent repo's full self-test build, not this worktree. So `sig build test-link [-Dlink-snapshot-update]` cannot run from this worktree in-env (confirmed: `error: unknown step 'test-link'`).
  3. An sBPF .so additionally needs `-target sbf-solana-solana -mcpu sbpfv3`, unavailable in-env (same as FEAT-002/003/004).
The ELF verifyObjdump cases are therefore in place and correct for CI (which can add an ELF target to the matrix); CI should run `sig build test-link -Dlink-snapshot-update` once to generate test/link/snapshots/elf-objdump.*.<arch>.dmp (and the sBPF -d case when the Solana target is available), then `sig build test-link` to confirm green with COFF snapshots unchanged.
